body:
Group: R10-FLOW-DISPATCH (PR #2577). No issue closed (`issues: []`). The PR adds the group path to `tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py`: `dispatch_group()` and `--group` render one seat from the roster, publish it to `dispatch/<role>-<topic>` on origin and print that ref name; the payload is the flag path's byte for byte (`render` is shared).

The class this head closes: a flag the parser accepts that the `--group` path neither consumes nor refuses. `--topic`, `--brief`, `--repo`, `--env-id` and `--out` were accepted under `--group`, dropped, and exit 0. `GROUP_FLAGS` now gives every parser flag its `--group` disposition: `None` when `main()` forwards it to `dispatch_group`, else the reason it refuses. `main()` refuses (exit 2, nothing dispatched) any refused flag set off its parser default. The parser moved into `_parser()` so the self-test reads the same parser `main()` uses. One table-driven self-test, `_flag_checks`, enumerates `_parser()._actions` and drives every flag through `main()` with `dispatch_group` stubbed to record its call. A flag missing from `GROUP_FLAGS` fails `every flag the parser accepts has a --group disposition in GROUP_FLAGS, and no other`. A forwarded flag whose value does not reach the call fails `--group forwards --<flag> to dispatch_group`. A refused flag that dispatches fails `--group refuses --<flag> (exit 2, nothing dispatched)`. The five are refused, not forwarded, because the group path's design is that the roster gives the topic, brief and repository, the seat environment gives the environment id, and the output is the ref. Forwarding `--env-id` was the alternative. It lost because a second source of the environment on the group path is a second owner of a concept the overlay already owns, and refusal keeps the group path's inputs exactly what its docstring states. The reviewer CLI fixture's pr is now `81`, two digits, so a truncated pr fails a named check too.

Reviewer refusal arms, deferred to R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE. Both need train state this repo's `origin/main` does not yet classify. (a) Refuse a reviewer at a head where a required context's latest run concluded failure needs R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE's classifier, which is not on `origin/main`. (b) The roster carry "Revision 12 (orchestrator, 2026-10-21)" item (2): refuse a reviewer at a head that shares a hot file (`pr_args.sh`, `update_pr.sh`, `cloud_relay.sh`, `orchestrator_tick.py`, `r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py`) with an open pull request holding an unboarded merge verdict. It needs open-PR file lists, verdict-bus reads and the train's boarded state. R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE is the roster's one owner of state classification for the train, the merge seat and the tick, so "is there an unboarded merge verdict" is its call; a second reader built here would duplicate it. `dispatch_group("reviewer", ...)` therefore still renders for any head. Carry: R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE
Item (1) of the same carry is built: the reviewer prompt requires every observation to sit under `## Findings` with its own `Carry:`, pinned by `the reviewer is told to separate findings, each with its own Carry:, from evidence`. Carry: dismissed: built in this diff

## Head

`ccd5f0611d5a5ef7332c4db32f28b572943e0c53` merges main `b787c7d` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`731a1149157881915df065ee7717126e687aa3d1` merges main `16a8240` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`283348fe4484c8c46477435a7af9997c09783e8f` merges main `1602f93` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`d1bc4b59c2ff4adeaf83325b2b0cc741eb5c907b` merges main `07fcbee` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`9720cda1ebc3cb8304e62b5914910d54642e721a` merges the authored code head `9dcdfe948c13a44aed6b700e91862d071112da11` and then merges origin/main `93e6a63d2` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

9dcdfe948c13a44aed6b700e91862d071112da11 (code head on `handoff/r10-flow-dispatch`). It adds three commits over 1060a1f035db0bb84263080ec4b36343a742c870: fe6080b3e4c4cbb3517c3bc4749ed2281034606b merges `origin/main` 93e6a63d2855651448a2b8f677b392feddc03c99 (no conflict; main's tip committed 2026-10-22T01:13:02Z, measured at 2026-10-22T01:45Z), e96aaeff2ac0c6e81fd797db200d20c07349ad3b is the fix and its self-test, and 9dcdfe948c13a44aed6b700e91862d071112da11 updates INSTRUMENTS.md.

## Mutation proof

Instrument: `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_flow_dispatch_mutants.py`. Each mutant is one replacement in `cloud_dispatch.py`, applied alone. Then `cloud_dispatch.py --self-test` runs and the file is restored byte for byte. The fix's mutants, each with its failing checks at the head:
- group-refusal-off (`if why and getattr(args, dest)` -> `if False and ...`, the fix's predicate deleted): failed=5. These fail: `--group refuses --brief`, `--env-id`, `--out`, `--repo` and `--topic` `(exit 2, nothing dispatched)`.
- env-id-forwarded-as-none (`--env-id`'s table entry flipped to forwarded): failed=1, `--group forwards --env-id to dispatch_group`.
- flag-unlisted (a parser flag `--extra` added with no table entry): failed=2, `every flag the parser accepts has a --group disposition in GROUP_FLAGS, and no other` and `--group forwards --extra to dispatch_group`.
- cli-pr-truncated (`pr=args.pr` -> `pr=(args.pr or '')[:1]`): failed=2, `--group forwards --pr to dispatch_group` and `the --group CLI passes --role, --group, --model, --pr and --nonce through`.
Every forwarded-flag mutant (cli-role-fixed, cli-group-fixed, cli-model-fixed, cli-head-dropped, cli-roster-ref-dropped, cli-pr-dropped, cli-nonce-dropped, cli-overlay-dropped) is also killed by its own `--group forwards --<flag> to dispatch_group` check, beside the fixture checks. The full drive at the head: `RESULT mutants=27 survived=0`. parent-drop, topic-to-id and roster-repo-ignored are CRASHED (a self-test that died before its summary line; killed, but no check names the break).

The near-equivalent `ref_privacy.refusal` on a constant ref in `_publish` (privacy-checks-message-only) is not pinned: the commit message carries the same home path, and git's ref-name check stands behind `_REF_CHARS`. Carry: dismissed: home-path case caught by the message check (item bd9a4d57)
cli-model-check-off and flagpath-head-required-off are equivalent: render refuses a missing model and a non-hex head (rc=2), so neither yields a silent wrong result. Carry: dismissed: equivalent, the refusal is render's own

## Null control

The drive's M0, the file unmutated: `RESULT mutant=M0 failed=0 verdict=null-ok` at the head. `cloud_dispatch.py --self-test`: 66 checks, 0 failed at the head. The 14 checks over 1060a1f's 52 are `_flag_checks`: one table check and one per parser flag (13). The stub in `_flag_checks` is the check's own null control: each forwarded flag carries a value no other argument carries (`value-of-<dest>`, role `probe` against base `fixer`), so a value found in the recorded call can only have come from that flag. The finder's demo at 1060a1f (below) is the null control for the fix: the same input exits 0 and dispatches there.

## Figures

- Finder's harness, both ends: the fix reviewer's demo, `git show origin/review/2577:evidence/demo_dropped_flags.py` (sha1 affe53b68ea1c7d6c11bd65b69af69e570d311ea), run as `python3 -I demo_dropped_flags.py <worktree>/tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py`. At 1060a1f: `rc 0 stdout dispatch/x`, and each of the five values prints `DROPPED` with `dispatch_group` called. At the head: `cloud_dispatch: refused: --topic does not apply with --group: the roster gives the topic (the group's branch)`, `rc 2 stdout ` (empty), `forwarded []`: nothing dispatched. The demo passes all five flags at once and the first refusal stops it. The per-flag exit codes are the five `--group refuses --<flag>` self-test checks, each red under group-refusal-off.
- The fix reviewer's drive, `git show origin/review/2577:evidence/mydrive_r4.py` (sha1 27bf925976ff2c29006214733c7a4fe50b4b2bca), `python3 -I mydrive_r4.py <worktree>`. At 1060a1f: `RESULT mutants=9 survived=1` (pr-truncated-1, failed=0). At the head: `RESULT mutants=9 survived=0`, pr-truncated-1 failed=2. pr-none and nonce-none are CRASHED at both ends; M0 is null-ok at both. The worktrees were clean after each run (`git status --porcelain` empty).
- `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_flow_dispatch_mutants.py`: `RESULT mutants=27 survived=0`, M0 `failed=0` (python 3.11).
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py --self-test | tail -1`: `cloud_dispatch self-test: 66 checks, 0 failed`.
- Class seam rule (fixer.md step 8): every flag `main()`'s parser accepts is, under `--group`, either forwarded to `dispatch_group` or refused with exit 2. The enumerating rule is the parser itself, `_parser()._actions` less `help`, against `GROUP_FLAGS`: `python3 -I -c 'import importlib.util as u,sys; s=u.spec_from_file_location("cd",sys.argv[1]); m=u.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(m); [print(a.dest, {None: "forwarded"}.get(m.GROUP_FLAGS.get(a.dest, "UNLISTED"), "refused" if a.dest in m.GROUP_FLAGS else "UNLISTED")) for a in m._parser()._actions if a.dest != "help"]' tools/audit/seat/cloud_dispatch.py`. It prints 13 seams, none `UNLISTED`. Null control: the same command on a copy with `ap.add_argument("--extra")` added prints `extra UNLISTED`. The self-test runs the same enumeration and drives each seat, so a seam this table calls forwarded is checked to arrive. Each flag and its disposition:
  - `--role`, `--group`, `--model`, `--head`, `--roster-ref`, `--pr`, `--nonce`, `--overlay`: forwarded. Each is pinned by its `--group forwards --<flag> to dispatch_group` check and by the two fixture checks on the published ref (`the --group CLI passes --head and --roster-ref through`, `the --group CLI passes --role, --group, --model, --pr and --nonce through`).
  - `--topic`, `--brief`, `--repo`, `--env-id`, `--out`: refused, closed in this diff. Each is pinned by `--group refuses --<flag> (exit 2, nothing dispatched)`.
  The API half, `dispatch_group`'s own parameters, is pinned by the earlier checks: roster_ref default (roster-ref-main) and explicit (explicit-roster-ref-ignored), head default (head-from-roster-ref) and explicit (head-ignored), pr and nonce (the reviewer refusals and nonce-altered), environ (`an unknown environment refuses`), repo_dir (every fixture call).
- `D=$(mktemp -d); python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D"; cat "$D/scope.txt"`: `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run, 32 scoped out.` (6 changed files), runs `tests/entities.py`. `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub /opt/hpo/venv-ci/bin/python tests/entities.py | tail -1`: `ALL 2382 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`
- `run.sh`'s `run_always` lines (venv-ci python 3.14.7, `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub:custom_components:tests`): `tests/harness_headers.py` prints `ALL 109 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`; `tests/env_drift.py --claims-only origin/main` prints `claims hygiene: origin/main ok`; `tests/closure.py selftest` prints `ALL 124 closure shrink pins PASSED`; `tests/layout.py` prints `layout self-test: ok`.
- `python3 tests/structure.py | tail -1`: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED` (no budget touched)
- `python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff origin/main HEAD | tail -1`: `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL`
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/ref_privacy.py --check | tail -1`: `0 refused`; `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/tmp_paths.py --check | tail -1`: `0 refused`; `python3 -I tests/throwaway_git.py --check | tail -1`: `0 raw git init or clone site(s) refused`
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/pr/ci_predict.py --base origin/main | tail -1`: `CI PREDICT: no closures or fast red predicted`
- `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...HEAD --stat | tail -1`: `6 files changed, 495 insertions(+), 18 deletions(-)`. `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)...HEAD --stat -- VERSION RELEASE_NOTES.md custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/manifest.json tests/golden | wc -l` prints 0: `VERSION`, the manifest, `RELEASE_NOTES.md`, goldens and claim files are untouched.

## Red checks

From the check-runs API, per commit. 1060a1f035db0bb84263080ec4b36343a742c870 (the PR head this round starts from): 49 runs, all completed. One is `failure`, `nightly-status`; every other run is `success` or `skipped`. The commits this round adds (fe6080b3e, e96aaeff2, 9dcdfe948) are not yet on the PR branch, so they carry no check runs.
`nightly-status` grades `main`, not this branch; no change here reaches it. Carry: dismissed: grades main not this branch
`ci-ratchet` is red on main's first-parent ancestry (46e368127, 302f66571, b0f134142; success at 214350c42; no run yet at 93e6a63d2) and skipped on this PR. It measures CI's critical path and script count, and this diff touches no workflow and adds no script run. Carry: dismissed: grades main not this branch

Red history, which pr-contract reads across every commit between origin/main and this head: `policy-docs`, `env-matrix`, `instrument-self-tests`, `fast` failed on d1bc4b59, a recarry merge made on 2026-10-22 at policy-docs (03:00:32Z); env-matrix (03:02:16Z); instrument-self-tests (03:03:39Z); fast (3.14) (03:15:06Z). All four ran while main itself was red, from 02:52Z to 04:35Z, because dev/governance/roles/orchestrator.md was over its files_tokens cap (4515 against 4513). #2595 fixed that, merged at dcf12f490. All four failed on main's own commits in the same window: policy-docs at 02:52Z, env-matrix at 02:53Z, instrument-self-tests at 02:55Z, and fast (3.14). The later heads' runs of these checks are green, so this PR caused none of them. The cheaper detector already exists: main's own policy-docs run, which went red first. The standing gap is that the red-history rule does not discount a main-red window. Carry: R10-POLICY-LINT-FAMILY

## Forward-carry

- Seam with R10-ORCH-MACHINERY (K17): dispatch through `bus.sh dispatch` and the worker registry are that group's. Carry: R10-ORCH-MACHINERY (item 92bca45d)

Round 2 re-review (third pass over this group: round 1 blocked at 6684dee65, this is the fixer's round 2 plus a main merge). Measured at 69a429cfab2d02fd938ac13ef2893c520ca98f7a in a detached worktree. The merge base equals origin/main 1ebc737e7, and roles/ has not changed between them. Spec: the pack file R10-FLOW-DISPATCH.json at 30c57744a. Roster: origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster at 545184b96.

## Block

Round 1 blocked on the head-ignored mutant: an explicit `head` replaced by a ref's tip while 42 checks stayed green. Round 2 pinned that one argument but left the same class open on the other explicit source the round added. With the mutant `roster_ref = roster_lib.reader_ref(repo_dir, roster_ref)` -> `roster_lib.reader_ref(repo_dir, None)`, all 48 self-test checks pass. In a fixture where origin/main and the round roster branch carry different briefs, `dispatch_group(..., roster_ref="origin/main")` then publishes the round branch's brief instead of main's (ev/explicit_roster_ref_demo.txt: unmutated `MAIN`, mutant `BRANCH`). That is a silently wrong brief on the documented `--roster-ref REF` interface. The CLI `--group` path, which is the operator's entry point and prints the line a standing trigger is fired with, is not called by any check. Dropping its `--head` (`head=args.head or ""` -> `head=""`) or its `--roster-ref` (`roster_ref=args.roster_ref` -> `None`) also leaves 48/48 green. For a fixer, the dropped `--head` silently dispatches at main's tip. A mutant drive that pins only the named lines, while its sibling inputs on the same path stay unpinned, does not meet fixer.md's mutation proof. The cost is two or three checks in `_group_checks`: an explicit `roster_ref` reading the other roster's brief, and one `main(["--group", ...])` call with `--head` and `--roster-ref` asserting both reach the prompt.

## Findings

- Unpinned: `dispatch_group`'s explicit `roster_ref` (mutant explicit-roster-ref-ignored, failed=0). The demo shows the wrong brief is published. Evidence: ev/reviewer_mutants_head.txt, ev/explicit_roster_ref_demo.txt. Carry: dismissed: returned to the fixer in this blocked verdict (item 61800936)
- Unpinned: the CLI `--group` path's pass-through of `--head` and `--roster-ref` (mutants cli-head-dropped and cli-roster-ref-dropped, failed=0 each). No check invokes `main` with `--group`. Carry: dismissed: returned to the fixer in this blocked verdict (item 83f73eb7)
- Unpinned, lower weight: `_publish`'s fetch of an existing dispatch ref (mutant fetch-skipped, failed=0). It survives because the fixture dispatches from the clone that made the earlier commit, so the tip object is already local. From a second clone the `rev-parse <tip>^{tree}` refuses, which fails loudly rather than silently. A second-clone re-dispatch check would pin it. Carry: dismissed: returned to the fixer in this blocked verdict (item 695058e1)
- Near-equivalent mutant: running `_publish`'s `ref_privacy.refusal` on a constant ref instead of `ref` survives, because the commit message `dispatch: {ref}` carries the same home path and the message check catches it. Only the ref-only `_REF_CHARS` rule goes unexercised, and git's own ref-name check stands behind it. The brief's `if why` pin (privacy-off) is killed. Carry: dismissed: home-path case caught by the message check (item bd9a4d57)
- Body figure stale at this head: the body's `cloud_dispatch self-test: 46 checks, 0 failed` was measured at the code head 742ed664. At 69a429cf it prints 48 checks, 0 failed. Both added checks come from main (#2583's carry-section prompt checks; main 1ebc737e7 alone prints 32). Re-measured: 742ed664 prints 46. Carry: dismissed: main merge adds two checks (item 15632c35)
- The roster carry for the deferred arm (R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE, item b87aa9e4, at 545184b96) names the behaviour but no control, unlike the K17 carry's `Control:` clause (finding-propagation.md, "carry the control, not only the claim"). It also says "must land before #2577 review", which contradicts the deferral the orchestrator ruled under mandate 6319294694. Suggested control: a reviewer dispatch at a head whose required context's latest run concluded failure refuses and pushes nothing, and the same head with that run green renders. Carry: R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE (item 1fb1501b)

## Evidence

- The deferral is disclosed: the body states the revision-7 reviewer refusal arm is not built, says why (R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE's classifier is not on origin/main; building it on the check-runs API would duplicate that concept, fixer.md step 17), says `dispatch_group("reviewer", ...)` still renders for any head, and carries it as `Carry: R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE (item b87aa9e4)`. That item is on the roster branch, and 58bf922e is its ancestor. Judged as the orchestrator directed: the disclosure is adequate. The carry text is the subject of the last finding above.
- The K17 seam carry (item 92bca45d) is on R10-ORCH-MACHINERY at the roster branch, and 903d137b is its ancestor. It now names both the bus.sh `dispatch` reviewer-fire close and the worker registry, and states `Control: a dispatch through dispatch_group leaves a reviewer-fire close in the ledger`. This settles round 1's workers.json item.
- Roster-ref and head separation pin: the check "by default the brief is the round's roster branch's and the head is main's tip, not that branch's" fails under roster-ref-main and head-from-roster-ref (failed=1 each). Its fixture puts the roster branch one commit ahead of main with its own brief. Confirmed.
- Survivor pins: head-ignored failed=1 and privacy-off failed=1, both killed. Confirmed.
- Brief-drop figure: failed=5 at this head, naming the five checks the body lists. Confirmed.
- The fixer's drive at this head (ev/fixer_drive_head.txt): M0 failed=0 null-ok; `RESULT mutants=13 survived=0`. Every per-mutant figure matches the body: tree-skip 2, brief-drop 5, nonce-altered 1, prompt-wrong 4, render-host-off 5, reviewer-head-off 1, roster-ref-main 1, head-from-roster-ref 1. topic-to-id, parent-drop and roster-repo-ignored all CRASHED (failed=-1).
- My own drive (ev/mydrive.py, ev/reviewer_mutants_head.txt): 10 mutants, 7 survived. Three of the survivors are judged equivalent: flagpath-head-required-off (render refuses a non-hex head, exit 2, demonstrated), cli-model-check-off (render refuses a missing model, its own check), and privacy-checks-message-only. The other four are the findings above. reviewer-guard-any-role and group-missing-no-refuse CRASHED (killed), and head-ignored-reviewer-only was killed by a named check.
- Figures re-derived at this head (ev/figures.txt): `MODE: SCOPED -- 1 script(s) run` (6 changed files); entities `ALL 2382 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED`; `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`; `Architecture score: dS +0.0000 NULL`; ref_privacy 0 refused (cloud_dispatch.py GUARDED); tmp_paths 0 refused; throwaway_git 0 refused; `ALL 109 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`; `claims hygiene: origin/main ok`. This is round 5. Rounds 1 to 4 blocked, the last at 1060a1f035db0bb84263080ec4b36343a742c870 with class-open (the `--group` CLI accepted `--env-id`, `--brief`, `--topic`, `--repo` and `--out`, dropped them, and exited 0). The finder's harness is the round-4 reviewer's demo and drive from origin/review/2577 (ea561e6ca): demo_dropped_flags.py (sha1 affe53b68) and mydrive_r4.py (sha1 27bf92597). ## Findings

- The round-4 roster carry item (2), the hot-file reviewer refusal arm (refuse a reviewer at a head that shares pr_args.sh, update_pr.sh, cloud_relay.sh, orchestrator_tick.py or r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py with an open pull request holding an unboarded merge verdict), is now deferred in the body to R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE, beside arm (a). Its routing is valid: carry_audit reports 0 unrouted, and R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE is live at stage not-started. But that group's roster `carry` at 306a96d5f holds only arm (a), as item b87aa9e4, with its control. Arm (b) is not on it yet, and the body states no control for (b). Before the merge it has to be written into R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE's roster carry with a control. A suitable control: a reviewer dispatch at a head sharing a hot file with an open PR that holds an unboarded merge verdict refuses, and the same dispatch with the verdict boarded passes. Carry: R10-FLOW-MAIN-GATE
- Surviving mutant refusal-truthy: `getattr(args, dest) != ap.get_default(dest)` -> `getattr(args, dest)`, failed=0. It is equivalent on every live input. It differs only for an explicitly empty value (`--brief ""`, `--env-id ""` and so on), and the flag path also reads an empty value as "absent" (`if args.brief`), so no seat changes.
